cards.text: This psalm is from David, the shepherd who became king of Israel. And who's the first one he preaches to? HIMSELF: "Bless the LORD, O my soul; all that is within me, bless His holy name."
Friend, I had LONG talks with myself in the back of a junk drawer, so I respect this man. David tells his soul to bless the LORD again, but this time he adds something his soul is NOT allowed to do.

cards.question: David tells his soul to bless the LORD. What does he tell his soul NOT to do?

answers.text: Grow tired of waiting on Him

cards.text: So David starts listing those kind deeds, talking right to his soul. And he opens with the big ones.

cards.question: David reminds his soul that the LORD ___ all your iniquities and ___ all your diseases.

cards.text: And the list keeps coming. The LORD redeems your life from the Pit, and friend, a stamper who got pulled out of a dark drawer knows EXACTLY how good that sounds.

cards.question: David says the LORD redeems your life from the Pit. Then He crowns you. With what?
David says the LORD satisfies you with good things, so that your youth is renewed. Renewed like the youth of which creature?

cards.text: Youth renewed like the eagle's. Friend, I came out of that drawer with SHARP edges and a FULLER mustache, but I promise you this gold base is not flying anywhere.
Then David zooms out past his own soul. He says the LORD executes righteousness and justice.

cards.question: David says the LORD executes righteousness and justice only for the people of Israel.
David says the LORD made His deeds known to the people of Israel. Who did He make His ways known to?
David says the LORD is compassionate and gracious, ___ to anger, abounding in loving devotion.

cards.text: Slow to anger. Friend, I have NOT been slow to anger with an oven timer that went off early, but the LORD will not always accuse us, nor harbor His anger forever.

cards.question: David says the LORD has not repaid us according to our iniquities.

cards.text: Not dealt with according to our sins. Not repaid according to our iniquities. Friend, David's soul is just getting WARMED up.
Now David reaches for pictures to show how big the LORD's loving devotion is for those who fear Him. Get ready, friend, these are BIG.

cards.question: How great does David say the LORD's loving devotion is for those who fear Him?

answers.text: As high as the heavens are above the earth
As deep as the sea is below the land
As wide as the desert is long

cards.question: David's next picture is about our transgressions. How far has the LORD removed them from us?

answers.text: As far as the east is from the west
As far as the sea is from the mountains
As far as the desert is from the city

cards.text: East from west. Friend, you can head west your WHOLE life and never once pass a sign that says "West Ends Here."

cards.question: David says the LORD has compassion on those who fear Him, the way a ___ has compassion on his children.

cards.text: A father with compassion on his children. Friend, I used to catch my six little cutters with my mustache every time they wobbled near the edge of the counter, so I FEEL this one.

cards.question: David says the LORD forgets what we are made of.

cards.text: He knows our frame. He is mindful that we are dust, and friend, after years in the back of a drawer, I can tell you dust is NOT a flex.
Then David looks at how short a person's days are. He says man's days are like grass, and he blooms like a flower of the field.

cards.question: David says that when the wind passes over the flower of the field, it grows back stronger.

cards.text: It vanishes, and its place remembers it no more. Wind comes, flower's gone, but David isn't done.

cards.question: Next to that flower that vanishes, how long does David say the LORD's loving devotion extends to those who fear Him?

answers.text: For as long as they live

cards.question: David says the LORD's righteousness reaches all the way to the children's children of those who fear Him.

cards.text: That's for those who keep His covenant and remember to obey His precepts. Then David looks up to where the LORD reigns.

cards.question: David says the LORD has established His ___ in heaven, and His kingdom rules over ___.

cards.text: Now David turns from his own soul and calls out to others to bless the LORD. And he starts with some heavy hitters.

cards.question: Who does David call to bless the LORD, the ones mighty in strength who carry out His word?

cards.text: Then he calls all His hosts, the servants who do His will, and all His works in all places of His dominion. Friend, that's EVERYBODY.

cards.question: After calling the angels, the hosts and all His works, who does David come back to at the very end of the psalm?

cards.text: "Bless the LORD, O my soul!" He calls out the angels and all His works, then circles right back home to his own soul, and friend, THAT is how you close out a psalm.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new backstory detail: Papa Dorin having long talks with himself in the junk drawer. The backstory says he didn't talk much during that time, and nothing in it mentions him talking to himself. Jokes may make up small moments around his bakery, not new facts about the drawer.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: This card only repeats 'Youth renewed like the eagle's', which card 8 already gave as its answer, and adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage and doesn't move it forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: Verse 6 says the LORD executes righteousness and justice 'for all the oppressed'. No card ever tells the baker who it is for. Card 10 stops before that phrase, and this True/False only rules out 'only for the people of Israel'. The baker leaves without a key detail of the verse.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This card is only 'East from west' plus a joke. It repeats card 3's answer and tells no new part of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This card only repeats card 5's answer ('A father with compassion on his children') and adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: This card asks about the closing 'Bless the LORD, O my soul!' in verse 22. That is the psalm's repeated line, which already appeared in verses 1 and 2 and was quoted on stop 1, card 1.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.
